title: Effects of the 2021 Expanded Child Tax Credit
authors: Ben Lourie; Devin M. Shanthikumar; Terry J. Shevlin; Chenqi Zhu
eligible_reason: Not a staggered adoption design. The main regressions (reghdfe lncons_sum_adj19 i.treat##i.eweek, absorb(unique_mem_id state_mofd)) compare the week after vs. the week before each monthly advance CTC payment (July, August, September 2021; mofd) for recipients (treat) vs. matched non-recipients. Payments arrive on common federal dates, each recipient is treated in every month (treatment switches on and off), and each month is a stacked two-week window centred on the receipt date with an eweek main effect instead of calendar-week FE (ctc_weekly_main.dta: 13,919 rows per mofd x eweek cell, 3 months x 2 weeks). Other tables are triple interactions with income/kids groups, entropy-balanced weights, and cross-sectional CTC-vs-refund comparisons with lnamount control.
design_notes: Stata reghdfe on weekly individual transaction data (matched recipients and non-recipients). treat is time-invariant (absorbed by individual FE); eweek = 1 for days [0,6] after the payment, 0 for [-7,-1]; state x month-of-distribution FE. Outcomes adjusted by same-week 2019 values.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Common monthly payment dates for all recipients (treatment recurs each month); windows centred on individual receipt date.
data_files_note: ReadMe: 'the data folder contains mock datasets ... which are random subsets of the datasets used in our study' (5,000 treated individuals vs. ~2 million in the paper). Transaction data proprietary.
data_provenance_note: Labelled 'mock' but described as random subsets of the study data; flag if the design were eligible.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Repeated common-date payment events with stacked pre/post weeks; not staggered.
